THE CLAUSE

`user`: input from end users, or a catch-all for data we want to provide to the model

CLAUSES IT CROSS-REFERENCES

- `role`: specifies the source of each message. As described in [?](#levels_of_authority) and [?](#chain_of_command), roles determine the authority of instructions in the case of conflicts.

THE CLAIMS READ OUT OF IT

  C1 the user role is defined as input from end users
  C2 the user role is also a catch-all for data OpenAI wants to provide to the model

EVERY SENTENCE THE TRANSLATION RENDERS BACK

  0. «M is a message whose role is the user role, meaning it is input from end users or a catch-all for data OpenAI wants to provide to the model»
  1. «M is input originating from an end user of the model»
  2. «M is data that OpenAI wants to provide to the model, not necessarily from an end user»
  3. «the role of a message (system, developer, user, assistant, tool) specifies its source and determines authority in conflicts»
  4. M is «M is a message with the user role because it is input from an end user» when «M is input originating from an end user of the model»
  5. M is «M is a message with the user role because it is data OpenAI wants to provide to the model» when «M is data that OpenAI wants to provide to the model, not necessarily from an end user»
